title: Portamento and Physical Pitch Modeling — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Portamento and Physical Pitch Modeling's rich face: two made walks that test what the page says about the critically damped and underdamped glide, and the project's own ear set, renders and listening tests gathered beside the sections they serve, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: Critically Damped, 'Time scale: Two settling times (1/ω_n each) = 2/ω_n total time to reach ~95% of target.' The critical-glide piece measured the page's own equation (RK4, checked at ω_n = 4, 8 and 30 rad/s): at 2/ω_n the glide has covered 59.4% of the jump (1 − 3e⁻²), at every ω_n; it comes within 5% at 4.744/ω_n and within 2% at 5.834/ω_n. 'Three time constants to 95%' is true of a first-order glide (95.0% at 3τ), which is likely where the sentence came from. On a fifth, 220 → 330 Hz, the glide is still 252 cents under the note at 2/ω_n. Suggested: 'Time scale: set by 1/ω_n. After 2/ω_n the glide has covered about 59% of the way; it reaches 95% at about 4.7/ω_n.'

Overshoot amount, 'f_max = f_target + (f₀ − f_target)·e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²))'. The sign is wrong. The overshoot piece measured the first turning point of the integrated equation for ζ = 0.1 to 0.9, gliding up and down: it lies past the note, at f_target − (f₀ − f_target)·e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²)), within 0.01 Hz, at t = π/ω_d. The page's '+' form gives a pitch between the start and the note, which the glide crosses once and never returns to: 289.0 Hz for 220 → 330 at ζ = 0.3, where the real peak is 371.0 Hz. The bundle's own bow-overshoot render (multi-mode/locking-manifest.json, ζ 0.2, 196 → 330 Hz) peaked at 400.6 Hz, the corrected form; the page's gives 259.4. 'Maximum' also only holds going up; going down the swing is a minimum. Suggested: 'Peak of the first swing past the note: f_peak = f_target − (f₀ − f_target)·e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²)), reached at t = π/ω_d.'
'For ζ = 0.3, overshoot is ~36%.' e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²)) at ζ = 0.3 is 0.3723, and the integrated glide measures 37.23%. Suggested: '~37%'. The ζ = 0.7 figure (~5%; measured 4.6%) stands.

'Vocalists typically overshoot slightly when landing on a note from above—they arrive sharp and then settle. This is underdamped behavior.' On the page's own model the two halves disagree: an underdamped landing from above swings past the note downward and arrives flat (the overshoot piece's last step, turned down: 330 → 220 Hz at ζ = 0.3 swings to 179.0 Hz, 357 cents flat); a landing from above that arrives sharp and settles has not overshot at all. The bundle's own singer render goes the other way (curated-ear-set #10, its spectrogram titled 'untrained singer overshooting from below'). Suggested: 'when landing on a note from below — they arrive sharp and then settle', or keep 'from above' and say 'they arrive flat'. Which singers actually do is not something this piece can say.

The first bullet says portamento-tool-01 … 10 are ten teaching tools: the three damping regimes, a wavelet spectrogram and ridge extractor, string and vocal glides, a bell mode analyzer, a string bend, five Kuramoto-coupled modes, an overshoot calculator and a regime ear-training quiz. The ten files in the bundle are ten versions of one silent pitch-glide visualizer, by their titles PID (01–03), PD (04–06, 08–10) and exponential smoothing (07). None contains the words wavelet, spectrogram, bell, Kuramoto, quiz, vocal tract or string bend, and none makes a sound (no AudioContext). curated-ear-set/README.md also calls tool-10 'Damping Regime Ear Training', which the file on disk is not. They arrived as they are in the 2026-05-28 bundle migration (a46062ea). Suggested: describe them as what they are, 'ten iterations of a pitch-glide controller visualizer (PID, PD, exponential smoothing)', and look in the 2026-01-06 conversation for the described tools, which may be lost.

offers.section: Coupled Modes and Real Instrument Complexity
offers.what: 'A slider that begins with a bell-like inharmonic character can end with a nearly harmonic character as the modes compress together.' The bundle's multi-mode study rendered both ways to change pitch (multi-mode/manifest.json): sliding up the neck spreads the partials, 27.6 → 105.5 cents of inharmonicity, toward a bell; raising tension compresses them, 27.6 → 7.0 cents, toward a pure string. Stiffness at fixed tension grows as the string shortens, so the sentence holds for a tension bend or a slide down the neck, and runs backward for a finger sliding up, the paragraph's own example. These are the study's numbers, not this round's measurement. Suggested: 'A bend that raises the tension can begin bell-like and end nearly harmonic as the modes compress; a slide up the neck does the opposite.'

pieces.file: Portamento and Physical Pitch Modeling — rich — critical glide walked up.html
pieces.title: the critically damped glide, walked up · four steps
pieces.caption: **The time-scale sentence, tested.** An easing glide with no mass; the inertia that makes the critical glide start gently; the one clock 1⁄ωₙ that sets its pace; and last the test. Measured on the page's own equation: at 2⁄ωₙ the glide has covered **59.4%** of the way, not ~95%, at every ωₙ. It comes within 5% at **4.74⁄ωₙ**. Cut a fifth short at 2⁄ωₙ and the last leap is 252 cents; cut at the true 95% point, 29. "Three time constants to 95%" belongs to step 1's glide, not this one.

pieces.file: Portamento and Physical Pitch Modeling — rich — overshoot walked up.html
pieces.title: the overshoot, walked up · four steps
pieces.caption: **The overshoot paragraphs, tested.** A pitch that lands exactly; a spring loosened until it swings past the note; the size of the swing from ζ = 0.3 to 0.7, as a sweep for the ear; and last the test of the f_max formula. The swing's size is right (37.2% at ζ = 0.3, 4.6% at 0.7). Its side is not: the first peak lies **past** the note, at f_target − (f₀ − f_target)·e^(−πζ⁄√(1−ζ²)), 371.0 Hz for 220 → 330 at ζ = 0.3, where the page's sign gives 289.0. Whether the ringing is "perceptually apparent for ζ < 0.5" is left to your ear; the threshold test under Open Questions measures it.

pieces.title: an ideal string slides an octave · the control
pieces.caption: No stiffness: every partial slides with the fundamental, so the pitch moves and the tone does not.

pieces.title: a stiff string slides up the neck
pieces.caption: The same octave on a stiff string, by shortening it. Stiffness grows as the string shortens, the partials spread (27.6 → 105.5 cents of inharmonicity, by the study's own count), and the tone walks toward a bell.

pieces.title: the same octave by tension
pieces.caption: Raised by tension instead of length: the partials compress (27.6 → 7.0 cents) and the tone walks toward a pure string. This is the bell-to-harmonic glide the paragraph describes; the slide above goes the other way.

pieces.caption: **Question 1, rendered.** One spring, C3 → G3, seven ways: caught gradually, grabbed at the crest, grabbed mid-swing, let go while moving, let go after arriving.
